key_insight: CorDex can synthesize large, task-relevant dexterous grasp datasets from a single human demonstration and learn to produce functional grasps for novel objects by combining semantic and geometric reasoning.
problem_solved: Overcomes the scarcity of large-scale dexterous grasping data and the lack of integrated semantic + geometric reasoning in models, enabling few-shot functional grasp learning.
method: Generate: procedurally create diverse synthetic grasp examples and object variations from one human demonstration.
Transfer: map semantic intent and geometric correspondences from the demonstrated object to novel objects to propose candidate grasps.
Adapt: refine transferred grasps with physics-aware and model-based adaptation (simulation-guided or learned refinement) to ensure functional success.
impact: Enables data-efficient training of dexterous grasp policies and reduces reliance on extensive real-world datasets, accelerating research and deployment of tool use and complex manipulation with robotic hands.

paper_title: Generate, Transfer, Adapt: Learning Functional Dexterous Grasping from a Single Human Demonstration
paper_authors: Xingyi He, Adhitya Polavaram, Yunhao Cao, Om Deshmukh, Tianrui Wang
